subject.title: fix(codex): reject hex/exponent computer wait duration strings

question: Should the Codex computer watchdog preserve decimal integer strings while rejecting other JavaScript-coercible strings, or should it mirror a number-only computer-tool contract?
rationale: The patch deliberately changes accepted input grammar, while the public documentation only says duration is measured in seconds and the generic Codex transport carries arbitrary JSON; maintainer intent is needed to select the permanent compatibility boundary.

options.title: Verify and mirror the executor contract
options.body: Inspect the computer tool schema and executor, then make the watchdog accept exactly the same duration forms and add parity coverage.

options.title: Accept decimal-string compatibility
options.body: Keep decimal integer strings as a named compatibility allowance while explicitly rejecting hexadecimal, exponent, fractional-string, and whitespace forms.

recommendation.title: Verify and mirror the executor contract
recommendation.body: Inspect the computer tool schema and executor, then make the watchdog accept exactly the same duration forms and add parity coverage.
